grammar.label: verb + noun collocations — take issue, draw a distinction, reach a conclusion
grammar.meaning: the noun carries the meaning; the verb is fixed by usage

explanation.en: English fixes which verb goes with which noun: you 'draw' a distinction, 'reach' a conclusion, 'take' issue, 'raise' an objection, 'meet' a requirement. The wrong verb is understood but marks the writer as non-native faster than a grammar error does.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tilida qaysi fe'l qaysi ot bilan kelishi qat'iy belgilangan. Noto'g'ri fe'l tushunarli bo'ladi, lekin grammatik xatodan ko'ra ko'proq ko'zga tashlanadi.

grammar.positive_example: The report draws a clear distinction between the two cases.
grammar.negative_example: The report makes a clear distinction between the two cases, so it does a conclusion.

l1_notes.uz: Lug'at tarjimasi kollokatsiyani ko'rsatmaydi; har bir juftlikni alohida yodlash kerak.

grammar.label: binomials — fixed pairs joined by and or or

grammar.meaning: a two-word unit whose order cannot be reversed

explanation.uz: 'terms and conditions', 'law and order', 'trial and error' — bir butun birlik. Tartib faqat odat bilan belgilangan va o'zgartirilmaydi.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I wrote 'I make a distinction between morbidity and mortality'.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: You draw a distinction. You make a point, and you reach a conclusion.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: None that I can teach you. The words simply travel in pairs, and a learner has to meet the pairs.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: So 'take issue with' and not 'take problem with'.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: That one you already had. Where did you get it?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: From reading the same reports for two years.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And 'safe and sound'? Bobur says it every time the bus comes back.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Fixed in that order, like 'safe and sound' itself. Turn either one round and it stops being English.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'Sound and safe' sounds like a person who learned English from a list.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Which is how most of us learned it. The pairs come later, from use.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then my class will read one real report a week.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Better than any list I could write for them.
